review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the two cyclotomic Eisenstein theorems closely. I also searched Mathlib for existing monic-comp API and found only `Monic.comp_X_sub_C`, so there is no ready replacement for the `X + 1` case. In the IsIntegral section, the two large proofs share some small pieces: the `hndiv` definition, the `isIntegral_norm` step, and the `1 ≤ k` side condition used twice inside one proof. Those are short or sit inside a single proof, so I did not report them. My proposed helpers have not been compiled. In particular, the exact form of the goal after the `simp only` in the second theorem's constant-coefficient branch is inferred from the rewrite lemmas used.

findings.problem: The two theorems repeat three pieces of reasoning. (1) Lines 49-51 and 81-83 build the same prime-ideal `≠ ⊤` argument for `Monic.isEisensteinAt_of_mem_of_notMem`. (2) Lines 52-55 and 84-87 are the same monic proof for `(cyclotomic _ ℤ).comp (X + 1)`, differing only in the cyclotomic index. (3) Lines 73-77 and 116-120 are character-for-character the same tail. After the different constant-coefficient rewrites, both goals reduce to `¬ (p:ℤ)^2 ∣ (p:ℤ)`. Each branch then re-derives this by casting to ℕ, extracting a quotient `k`, proving `2 ≤ p` and `p < p^2`, and finishing with `cases k <;> grind`. Any change to the hypotheses of `isEisensteinAt_of_mem_of_notMem` or to the cast lemmas has to be made in both places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add three private lemmas before the first theorem.
1. `private lemma monic_cyclotomic_comp_X_add_one (n : ℕ) : ((cyclotomic n ℤ).comp (X + 1)).Monic`. Proof: `rw [show (X + 1 : ℤ[X]) = X + C 1 by simp]; refine (cyclotomic.monic n ℤ).comp (monic_X_add_C 1) fun h => ?_; rw [natDegree_X_add_C] at h; exact zero_ne_one h.symm`.
2. `private lemma not_sq_dvd_prime_int [hp : Fact p.Prime] : ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ 2 ∣ (p : ℤ)`. Proof: the existing tail, namely `intro h; obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Int.natCast_dvd_natCast.1 h; have := hp.out.two_le; have : p < p ^ 2 := by nlinarith; cases k <;> grind`.
3. A wrapper that bundles the prime-ideal `ne_top`: `private lemma isEisensteinAt_comp_X_add_one_of {f : ℤ[X]} [Fact p.Prime] (hf : f.Monic) (hmem : ∀ {i}, i < (f.comp (X + 1)).natDegree → (f.comp (X + 1)).coeff i ∈ 𝓟) (hnot : (f.comp (X + 1)).coeff 0 ∉ 𝓟 ^ 2) : (f.comp (X + 1)).IsEisensteinAt 𝓟`. Its body is `Monic.isEisensteinAt_of_mem_of_notMem (hf.comp ...) (Ideal.IsPrime.ne_top ...) hmem hnot`. It reuses the `Ideal.span_singleton_prime` expression once and can use the monic lemma from item 1.
The first theorem then becomes `isEisensteinAt_comp_X_add_one_of (cyclotomic.monic p ℤ) (fun {i hi} => <existing choose/binomial branch>) (by rw [coeff_zero_eq_eval_zero, eval_comp, cyclotomic_prime, ..., one_geom_sum, Ideal.submodule_span_eq, Ideal.span_singleton_pow, Ideal.mem_span_singleton]; exact not_sq_dvd_prime_int p)`. The second theorem becomes the same call with `cyclotomic.monic _ ℤ`, its induction branch, and its geometric-sum rewrite followed by `exact not_sq_dvd_prime_int p`. If the `Monic.comp` argument does not fit the wrapper, use item 1 directly.
findings.benefit: The two theorems are left with only what differs: the coefficient-divisibility argument and the evaluation of the constant coefficient. The non-obvious `p < p^2` / `cases k` argument gets a name and a statement and is written once. The prime-ideal and monicity boilerplate has a single place to maintain. A reader can see that both theorems follow the same Eisenstein pattern.
